correctness.rationale: For two effective projected nodes the Hankel determinant is c_1 c_2(u_1-u_2)^2, regardless of the total mass. The order-two recurrence gives exactly the displayed sum and product of nodes by Cramer's rule; the weights then come from an invertible Vandermonde system. A single effective node has nonzero total mass; a zero marginal has all four moments zero. Distinct two-dimensional atoms must separate along at least one of the two coordinates, so if neither axis has two effective nodes a feasible measure is one atom or zero. When both axes separate, unequal weights fix the pairing, or equal weights give two mixed moments differing by the nonzero product c(z_1-z_2)(w_1-w_2). A one-node partner fixes the common coordinate. A vanished partner forces opposite weights and a common coordinate; the first moment on the separating axis is then nonzero and the mixed ratio recovers the hidden coordinate. Invalid marginal discriminants, coefficients and moduli can be rejected, and recomputing all eight moments of the candidate establishes feasibility for arbitrary data. The equal-weight swap proves indistinguishability by every axial sample. Independent Gaussian-integer grid enumeration had 3081 distinct full signatures and 2757 distinct axial signatures, with every feasible marginal type present.
residual_risks: Exact input and arithmetic model; no noisy-data stability or global eight-sample minimality follows.
The bounded grid is a check, not the injectivity proof.

evidence: Corollary 10 establishes identifiability; the same paper's stated reconstruction theorem uses a larger set. Sauer gives multivariate Hankel interpolation with finite truncations. Cuyt–Lee give the Prony line method and the shifted Vandermonde equations (7)–(8), followed by division by the unshifted weight. Kunis et al. study a distinct Toeplitz approach.

evidence: For a valid two-atom input at least one axial 2-by-2 Hankel matrix is rank two since one coordinate separates. If it is x, take Δ=e_1 and δ=e_2 in (7)–(8). Ordinary Prony on (0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0) recovers z_j and c_j. Using (0,1),(1,1), (8) solves d_1+d_2=Y_1, z_1 d_1+z_2 d_2=H. It gives d_j=c_j w_j individually and division recovers w_j. There is no assumption that w_1 differs from w_2 or that Y_1, Y_0 are nonzero. If y separates, switch x and y; the union of inputs is precisely Ω.

The phase variables exp(Φ) and exp(Φ_shift) suffice as torus points, so the paper's subsequent logarithmic recovery and its Nyquist-strip restriction introduce no additional requirement. When neither axis separates, the at-most-two model leaves just zero or a singleton. Unit-modulus and eight-moment residual validation makes this recovery a membership test.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is a direct specialization with a rank-based choice between two already available orientations. The particular case table and weight-pairing implementation are a reformulation, not a new constructive result. Axis-only nonidentifiability is the elementary ambiguity of pairing two equal-weight marginals.

originality.rationale: Hyperbolic-cross uniqueness is already known, as the record acknowledges. The explicit inversion is also mechanically obtained from the existing Prony plus identification-shift equations: the fixed eight samples supply the two possible coordinate orderings of their six-sample distinct-projection design. Rank chooses a separating axis for every genuine two-atom measure. No collision-disentangling theorem or extra sampling is required once that axis is chosen, even if the other marginal completely cancels. The frozen pair-matching presentation is different but the constructive guarantee and feasibility follow directly.

value.rationale: The problem of a fixed exact torus sampling design is natural, and the algorithm can be a useful exposition. But its efficiency and degeneracy guarantees for this eight-sample design follow from the existing shift construction, an elementary branch choice, and residual checking. Neither a nontrivial new inversion theorem nor a global minimality result remains; the two-weight swap is a direct marginal ambiguity.
